title: Grateful Dead Live at San Diego International Sports Arena on 1973-11-14
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Samplitude Professional v7.02 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a stellar November‑1973 show highlighted by a blazing Here Comes Sunshine and an epic Truckin’ → The Other One jam marathon.
ai_review.review: The recording, benefitting from Charlie Miller’s superb upgrade, delivers crystal‑clear soundboard fidelity with only occasional minor slip‑ups. Musically the concert is celebrated for its monster second set – multiple reprises of The Other One, a soaring Eyes of the World, and a standout Here Comes Sunshine – while the first set offers solid classics despite some listeners finding it less adventurous. Overall the performance and tape quality earn universal praise.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews, most giving 5 stars and praising both the music and the soundboard transfer; only a few mixed comments do not outweigh the strong consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mix with great SQ thanks to Charlie Miller’s upgrade; occasional minor slip‑ups (e.g., a tiny HCS flub) but overall very clear and balanced.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set is solid but considered a bit pedestrian by some listeners; the second set explodes with extended jams and seamless segues, making it one of the most celebrated sets of the fall‑73 tour.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for tight playing, soaring lead tones, expressive vocals on Sugaree, and relentless soloing throughout the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Often highlighted for powerful bass ‘bombs’ and a raging rhythm foundation; occasional notes of him being “off‑the‑mark” or missing intensity in certain jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for lyrical slip‑ups (e.g., first verse of HCS) but praised for passionate vocal delivery.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano receives glowing remarks – described as monstrous, accurate, exploratory, and a key driver of the band’s energy during this period.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s syncopated off‑beat work is lauded; Billy (the second drummer) gets credit for creative, jazzy contributions throughout the extended jams.
